title: Workflow Recipe
description: Versioned data contract for an OAC workflow recipe (ADR-0016, Plan Step 6.2). A recipe is a named, versioned pipeline of phases and steps; each step names a command/ability and may declare a machine-evaluable artifact check (glob + required pattern) or a human `note` fallback when completion cannot be auto-detected.

schemaVersion.description: Recipe contract version. Bump when the phase/step shape changes.

description.description: One-to-two sentence summary of what the recipe does.

version.description: Semantic version of this recipe revision, e.g. '1.0.0'.

id.description: Unique kebab-case phase id within the recipe.

type.description: serial runs the phase's steps in order; parallel runs independent steps together.

dependsOn.description: Phase ids that must complete before this phase starts. Every entry must name a phase in this recipe.

id.description: Unique step id within its phase.

kind.description: How the step executes: route to an agent, wait on a human, invoke a command, run a CLI command, call an ability, or emit a report.

command.description: Slash command or CLI command the step runs.

agents.description: Agent ids the step routes to.

gates.description: Named gates that must be satisfied for the step.

artifact.description: Completion check. Machine-evaluable when `glob` is present: `minCount` (default 1) files must satisfy the check — the glob matches when `pattern` is absent, and matched files whose contents contain the regex when `pattern` is given (so `minCount` counts pattern-satisfying files, not all glob matches). `note` is the human fallback used only when completion cannot be auto-detected; it is mutually exclusive with `glob`.

glob.description: Machine-evaluable file glob, relative to the project root.

pattern.description: Machine-evaluable regex that must appear in each counted matched file (requires `glob`).

minCount.description: Machine-evaluable minimum number of matched files (default 1; requires `glob`).

note.description: Human fallback when completion cannot be auto-detected (used only when `glob` is absent).
